answer: An agent economy mints a fixed garden of 500 participation seats each epoch, sealed-bid and burned at a single clearing price set in basalt at settlement. A farm wanting 200 seats bids that price up and pays the raised anchor on all 200, so its 200th seat clears far above its first and the marginal cost bends upward the more it grabs, without the ledger ever attributing which alias belongs to whom. A thousand clones cannot pool into one cheap seat: every seat burns its own anchored bid and the next only climbs higher.
